clue.text: Get Castro in a tizzy introducing American items of clothing

indicators.note: introducing means one piece is brought into the middle of the other

explanation.surface: Someone flusters Fidel Castro by bringing in American garments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a tizzy' scrambles GETCASTRO, and 'introducing' puts A among those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Greatcoats are heavy overcoats, so they count as garments worn over other clothes.

clue.text: Fliers briefly split lottery

parts.note: the RAF, Britain's Royal Air Force, is a body of fliers

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short, losing its final letter

parts.note: to split is slang for to leave in a hurry, to flee

explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' docks the last letter of FLEE to give FLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A raffle is a prize draw in which numbered tickets are sold, a kind of lottery.

clue.text: Elkie's singer quietly leaves nobleman

indicators.note: leaves means that letter goes away from the word

parts.note: Elkie Brooks had a hit with 'Pearl's a Singer', so her singer is Pearl
P, for piano, is the musical direction meaning quietly

explanation.surface: A singer slips quietly out of the room, leaving a nobleman behind.
explanation.walkthrough: Elkie Brooks is a British singer whose 1977 hit was 'Pearl's a Singer'; 'leaves' takes P out of PEARL.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is a British peer ranking above a viscount, so a titled nobleman.

clue.text: Type of marble style in corridor

parts.note: an alley is a large playing marble, originally of alabaster
a way of doing something is its style or manner

explanation.surface: A particular sort of marble decorates a passage.
explanation.definitionFit: An alleyway is a narrow passage between buildings, an outdoor corridor.

clue.text: Register for work

definitions.meaning: a cash register in a shop
to work the soil by ploughing

explanation.surface: Someone signs on to find a job.
explanation.definitionFit: A till holds a shop's takings, and tilling land means cultivating it for crops.

clue.text: Take in Indian spices and wine

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the spice word

parts.note: masala is a blend of ground spices used in Indian cooking
R, from Latin recipe, is the abbreviation for take on a prescription

explanation.surface: A cook takes in some Indian spices and a glass of wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take in' looks like one phrase, but Take gives R and 'in' puts it inside MASALA.
explanation.definitionFit: Marsala is a fortified wine from Sicily, often used in cooking.

clue.text: Look to incorporate zone for mast

indicators.note: to incorporate means the first word takes the second into its body

parts.note: a person's mien is their look or bearing

explanation.surface: Someone aims to bring a zone within sight of a ship's mast.
explanation.definitionFit: The mizen is the mast nearest the stern on a ship with three or more masts.

clue.text: Landowner involved in tactical air defence

indicators.note: involved in says the answer is wrapped up within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A landowner takes part in planning a battlefield air defence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved in' points to the run tacticaL AIR Defence.
explanation.definitionFit: A laird is a Scottish owner of a landed estate.

clue.text: Hardy expert supports Durham

indicators.note: in a down answer, a piece that supports another sits below it

parts.note: Dur is an abbreviation for the county of Durham
able means skilled or expert

explanation.surface: A specialist on Thomas Hardy backs a team from Durham.
explanation.walkthrough: Durham is a county in north-east England; 'supports' puts ABLE under DUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hardy withstands rough conditions, which is what durable means.

clue.text: American poet has time to pen final letter

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so the time word holds the letter

parts.note: an era is a period of time
Z is the last letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: A US poet has a moment to write the last letter of a correspondence.
explanation.definitionFit: Ezra Pound was a leading American modernist poet, known by his first name here.

clue.text: River creature with weapon creates unnecessary panic

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall
a seal is a sea creature
an arm is a weapon, as in firearm

explanation.surface: An armed animal emerging from a river causes needless alarm.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fal is a river in Cornwall, south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: A false alarm is a warning of danger that turns out to be groundless.

clue.text: Underwear thief in Kansas

indicators.note: in places the thief inside the state abbreviation

parts.note: KS is the postal abbreviation for Kansas
to nick is British slang for to steal, so a nicker is a thief

explanation.surface: A lingerie thief is on the loose in Kansas.
explanation.definitionFit: Knickers is the British word for women's pants, an item of underwear.

clue.text: Special border plant

parts.note: an edge is a border

explanation.surface: A gardener picks a particular plant for the border.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedge is a grass-like plant growing in wet ground.

clue.text: Used to be part of the LGBT community, which is quite spicy

definitions.note: the definition describes a thing: the answer is a hot condiment

parts.note: was is the past tense of be
a bi, short for a bisexual person, is one member of the B in LGBT

explanation.surface: Someone was once in the LGBT community, a racy past.
explanation.definitionFit: Wasabi is a pungent Japanese horseradish paste, notably hot on the tongue.

clue.text: Details of money everyone found in career

indicators.note: found in means these pieces are set inside the other word

parts.note: to career is to rush along, as in a sprint
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Particulars about how much everyone earns in their profession.
explanation.walkthrough: 'career' looks like a noun meaning profession, but it is the verb, to rush.
explanation.definitionFit: Small print is the fine detail of a contract, often overlooked.

clue.text: Furniture store with department covering Kelvin's proposal

indicators.note: covering means one letter lies over another, hiding it and taking its place

parts.note: IKEA is the Swedish furniture chain
K is the symbol for the kelvin, the unit of temperature

explanation.surface: A furniture store's department presents Kelvin's suggestion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' puts D over the K of IKEA, replacing it.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea is a thought put forward, a suggestion or proposal.

clue.text: Spoken to without notice to be prepared

parts.note: to address someone is to speak to them
an ad, short for advertisement, is a notice

explanation.surface: Someone is told to get ready at no notice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes AD from the front of ADDRESSED.
explanation.definitionFit: Food is dressed when it is prepared for the table, as with a dressed crab or salad.

clue.text: Religious measure accepted by artist leaving America

indicators.note: accepted by means the measure is taken into the other piece
leaving means that letter departs from the artist's name

dl, the decilitre, is a measure of volume

explanation.surface: An artist who has left America takes on a devout measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' leaves GOY, which then holds the measure; the decilitre is a metric unit solvers may not think of as a measure word.

clue.text: Courageous person follows criminal group into nerve centre

indicators.note: follows means the brave person comes after the group

parts.note: a gang is a group of criminals
a lion is a brave person

explanation.surface: A brave detective tails a gang into its headquarters.
explanation.definitionFit: A ganglion is a cluster of nerve cells, a literal nerve centre.

clue.text: Air defence space in port

parts.note: an en is a printer's space, half an em

explanation.surface: Air defences are set up in a harbour area.
explanation.walkthrough: An en is a printing measure of space.
explanation.definitionFit: Aden is a seaport in Yemen at the mouth of the Red Sea.

clue.text: The French native set exercise

parts.note: les is French for the, in the plural
a son is a native, as in a son of the soil

explanation.surface: A French teacher gives a homework task to a local pupil.
explanation.definitionFit: A lesson can be a piece of work given to a student, such as a passage set to learn.

clue.text: Presumably released from incarceration and did very well

definitions.meaning: read as ..., formerly held in a cell

explanation.surface: An ex-prisoner made a success of life.

explanation.definitionFit: To excel is to be outstandingly good at something.

clue.text: Graduate invested in funds for African fortress

indicators.note: invested in means put inside, a pun on investing money

parts.note: cash is ready money or funds
a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: A graduate puts money into a fort in North Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A casbah is the citadel of a North African city, such as Algiers.

clue.text: Go in with some Aberdeen Terriers

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

clue.text: Lear boasts about old navigational aids

indicators.note: about means the letters are turned round and rearranged

explanation.definitionFit: Astrolabes were early instruments for measuring the height of stars, used by navigators before the sextant.

clue.text: Busy bee ignored hazard

indicators.note: ignored means that letter is passed over and left out

parts.note: brisk means busy, as in brisk trade
bee is the spoken name of the letter B

explanation.surface: A busy bee pays no attention to danger.
explanation.definitionFit: A risk is a danger or chance of harm, the same as a hazard.

clue.text: Report of grain in island

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the word is said out loud

parts.note: barley is a cereal grain

explanation.surface: News of a grain harvest on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: The match relies on a non-rhotic British accent, where the R in barley is not pronounced.
explanation.definitionFit: Bali is an Indonesian island east of Java.

clue.text: Heartlessly declaims traitors

indicators.note: heartlessly means the central letter is taken out

parts.note: to rant is to declaim loudly

explanation.surface: Someone coldly denounces those who betrayed them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartlessly' removes N, the middle letter of RANTS.
explanation.definitionFit: A rat is slang for someone who deserts or betrays their side.

clue.text: Periodically admits actor into dance

indicators.note: periodically means letters are taken at regular intervals, here every second one

explanation.surface: From time to time a club lets an actor into a dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Periodically' takes the second, fourth and every other letter: aDmItS aCtOr.
explanation.definitionFit: A disco is a party or club night with dancing to recorded pop music.

clue.text: Intern in NI town welcoming English rector

indicators.note: welcoming means the town takes the letter inside it

parts.note: Larne is a port town in County Antrim, Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A trainee in a Northern Irish town greets the English vicar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'welcoming' puts E inside LARNE to make LEARNE, then R follows.
